selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What are the two medicines in this passage?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah with patience, and depending on Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: When a person feels weak, who should he depend on?
questions.answer: He should depend on Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say a trusting person remembers during a hard trouble?
questions.answer: He remembers that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: How can knowing Allah change the way a person feels about being weak?
questions.answer: It can make him feel peace and even sweetness instead of only sadness.

questions.question: What baby example is given to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: A baby feels safe by running to its mother when afraid.

questions.question: Is a mother’s mercy bigger than Allah’s mercy, or only a tiny part of it?
questions.answer: It is only a tiny part of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Why do wise people say they have no real power by themselves?
questions.answer: Because they know all true strength comes from Allah.

questions.question: What do wise people use to draw near to Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: Their weakness and their fear of Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage teach people to be proud of themselves, or to seek Allah’s help?
questions.answer: It teaches them to seek Allah’s help.

questions.question: If a person thinks he is strong all by himself, would that match the lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: No. The passage teaches that people should know their need for Allah.

questions.question: What is the first medicine named in the passage?
questions.answer: Trust in Allah with patience.

questions.question: What is the second medicine named in the passage?
questions.answer: Relying on the Creator’s power and trusting His wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the passage say a person does not need to live in constant fear?
questions.answer: Because Allah is in control of everything.

questions.question: What should a believer do when a very hard problem happens?
questions.answer: He should turn to Allah and trust Him.

questions.question: What feeling can come from fearing Allah in the right way?
questions.answer: A good and comforting feeling can come from it.

questions.question: How does the story of the baby help us understand trusting Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that a weak one feels safe by taking refuge in the one who cares for him.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does the kindness of mothers really come from?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What have wise people chosen instead of trusting their own strength?
questions.answer: They choose to take refuge in Allah.

questions.question: Why do wise people admit they are powerless?
questions.answer: Because it helps them turn sincerely to Allah.

questions.question: What is the passage teaching about real strength?
questions.answer: Real strength is not in ourselves; it is in depending on Allah.

questions.question: Which two actions are called medicines here?
questions.answer: Patience with trust in Allah, and confidence in Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: What mighty ability of Allah is mentioned to show His power?
questions.answer: He can make things happen by His command.

questions.question: In the worst hardship, what does the trusting person do first?
questions.answer: He gives himself over to Allah and depends on Him.

questions.question: What kind of Lord does the passage describe Allah as for the person who trusts Him?
questions.answer: A very caring and merciful Lord.
